oneLineDefinition: The theoretical and mathematical foundation of computing, covering algorithms, data structures, computation theory, and the science behind how software and hardware work.
overview: Computer Science is the most academically rigorous technology major. It covers the mathematical and theoretical underpinnings of computing: algorithm design and analysis, computational complexity, operating systems, compiler design, and formal methods. It is the closest to a pure science degree in the technology field. Graduates have the strongest foundation for roles in research, systems programming, or fields requiring deep algorithmic thinking like AI and cryptography.
typicalProjects: Implement a sorting algorithm library with complexity analysis
Build a simple interpreter or compiler for a toy language
Implement core OS components (scheduler, memory allocator)
Solve competitive programming problems (Codeforces, LeetCode hard)
Research and implement a paper on a specific algorithm
requiredSkills: Mathematical proof writing and abstract thinking
Ability to analyze time and space complexity rigorously
Strong English for reading research papers and documentation
suitableFor: Students who enjoy abstract problem-solving and mathematical reasoning
Those interested in research, academia, or deep technical work
Students who want the strongest possible foundation for AI, systems, or cryptography
Competitive programmers who want to formalize their skills
notSuitableFor: Students who want to build products quickly and see immediate results
Those who dislike formal mathematics and proof-based thinking
Students who want a curriculum closely tied to current industry tools and frameworks
keyTakeaways: CS provides the most transferable foundation — graduates can enter almost any technical field
The curriculum is often disconnected from day-to-day industry work, requiring additional self-study
CS graduates are highly competitive at top tech companies (FAANG-style interviews heavily test CS fundamentals)
Strong CS knowledge significantly accelerates learning in AI and systems engineering
cautionNotes: CS programs vary widely — some are very theory-heavy with minimal industry preparation
Graduates often need to supplement with practical projects and internships
The 'best major for FAANG' reputation attracts students who may not enjoy the actual curriculum
marketDemand: Very high for graduates with strong fundamentals. CS graduates are preferred by top-tier tech companies for their rigorous training.
salaryOutlook: Similar to Software Engineering at entry level. CS graduates with strong algorithmic skills can command premium salaries at top tech firms. Research roles are more varied.
futureTrend: Strong fundamentals remain invaluable as AI tools automate surface-level coding. CS graduates are well-positioned for emerging areas like quantum computing, cryptography, and AI research.
commonMisconceptions: Computer Science is only about programming
CS is the same as Software Engineering — CS is more theoretical and academic
CS graduates mainly become programmers — many go into research, data science, or non-traditional tech roles
You need to be a genius to study CS — strong work ethic and mathematical curiosity matter more than innate talent

faq.question: Is Computer Science harder than Software Engineering?
faq.answer: Generally yes, especially in terms of mathematical rigor and theoretical content. SE focuses on building software; CS focuses on understanding how computing fundamentally works.
